Because newly detected cribriform tumours were exclusively MRI-visible, early repeat biopsy of patients with MRI-visible disease may considerably improve risk stratification.
n613bebf05581: Since its inception in 2003, the United States President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) has played a central role in HIV/AIDS prevention and treatment across Sub-Saharan Africa. Following the January 2025 suspension of United States foreign aid, which includes PEPFAR funding, countries across Sub-Saharan Africa demonstrated varying governmental responses to the resulting HIV funding disruptions. This study evaluates whether national characteristics were associated with a country's ability to respond to this funding crisis. Countries in Sub-Saharan Africa receiving PEPFAR funding were classified into one of three response categories: Level 1 (minimal or no governmental response), Level 2 (government response without sufficient plans or resources to fully offset funding losses), or Level 3 (high governmental response with strategies to maintain HIV/AIDS prevention and treatment services). Response categories were compared with national Human Development Index (HDI), GDP per capita, HIV prevalence, total population living with HIV, annual HIV mortality, and historical PEPFAR funding. Univariable proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with response level. Five countries (17.2%) were classified as Level 1, 10 (34.5%) as Level 2, and 14 (48.3%) as Level 3. Higher HDI was significantly associated with stronger governmental response (OR = 4.05; 95% CI, 1.49-11.04; Holm-adjusted p = 0.0376). GDP per capita (OR = 2.35; 95% CI, 1.00-5.51; unadjusted p = 0.0489) and HIV prevalence (OR = 3.53; 95% CI, 1.03-12.11; unadjusted p = 0.0452) demonstrated positive associations before adjustment for multiple comparisons, but neither remained significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.2261 for both). Historical PEPFAR funding, total population living with HIV, and annual HIV mortality were not significantly associated with response level after adjustment. Countries with higher levels of human development demonstrated stronger governmental responses to the 2025 PEPFAR funding disruptions. Several countries with minimal documented responses were also affected by active conflict or political instability, potentially compounding their vulnerability to treatment interruptions. These findings suggest that broader national development may play an important role in governmental responses to funding disruptions and highlight the need to strengthen resilient health systems, diversify HIV financing, and prioritize support for countries at greatest risk of future funding shocks.
n5676103b29ca: Background. Research data enclaves such as the All of Us Research Program do not allow participant-level data, or models fitted to them, to leave, which makes it hard to deliver case-finding models, which flag patients with possibly uncoded conditions for clinician review, to patients and clinicians. Objectives. We describe and technically evaluate a system that fits models outside an enclave from released summary counts and delivers them through standard health information technology interfaces. Methods. We exported dissemination-compliant summary counts from the All of Us Researcher Workbench and, outside the enclave, fitted versioned models for Long COVID, chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, endometriosis, Lyme disease, lupus, migraine, depression, and anxiety. A model contract (a model file and a written specification), a Python reference implementation, and synthetic Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) test patients define the expected outputs. One JavaScript scorer runs in a patient demonstration, a SMART on FHIR clinician application, and a CDS Hooks service. An atlas displays aggregate results. We evaluated the system on synthetic records with automated tests, cross-implementation output comparison, launches through the public SMART sandbox, and a counterexample review of the scoring and display rules. Results. The deployed Long COVID model had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.67 in a random validation split. The eight self-report models reached 0.61 to 0.82 in identifying self-reporters without a code. The JavaScript scorer reproduced all 162 reference outputs exactly, and all 437 automated tests passed. A counterexample review found 5 classes of failure, including scoring ineligible patients and treating unavailable data as absent, all fixed and added as tests. Conclusions. Models fitted from released summary counts can be delivered through FHIR, SMART on FHIR, and CDS Hooks with reproducible scoring on synthetic records. Real-record interoperability, usability, and prospective clinical performance remain to be evaluated.
n22b26336d685: Introduction: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) is a global public health problem and a major cause of mortality in low- and lower-middle-income countries. Human bocavirus (HBoV) is among the viral agents associated with this condition. Therefore, investigating the presence of HBoV in cases of AGE in Salvador, Bahia, as well as its prevalence and circulating strains, is important. Objective: To investigate the occurrence of HBoV infection during an AGE outbreak in Salvador. Methods: A total of 178 samples were analyzed for HBoV using nested polymerase chain reaction (nested PCR), and the amplification products were visualized by agarose gel electrophoresis. HBoV was detected in 5.7% of the samples analyzed. Conclusion: This study contributes to the understanding of HBoV epidemiology as a secondary agent associated with acute gastroenteritis during a norovirus outbreak in Salvador. Continued investigation and identification of the etiological agents involved in outbreaks are essential for evaluating the causes of AGE. These findings also highlight the need for broader diagnostic approaches and the importance of phylogenetic analysis for monitoring and controlling viral infections.
n8ac0312baed7: Introduction: Thyroid diseases are major health problems and among the most common endocrine disorders worldwide, including in Ethiopia. They are characterized by alterations in hormone secretion, enlargement of the thyroid gland, or both. Fine needle aspiration cytology is an important initial screening tool, and histopathologic examination is essential for the definitive diagnosis of thyroid disease. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy of fine needle aspiration cytology with histopathology in identifying thyroid diseases. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted at three health facilities in Hawassa City, Ethiopia, involving 304 patients who underwent both thyroid fine needle aspiration cytology and histopathologic examination of the same site between 30th October 2024 and 29th October 2025. FNAC results were classified using the Bethesda system, with histopathology as the gold standard. Data were entered into Kobo Toolbox, exported to SPSS version 27, and analyzed using cross-tabulation and chi-square ({chi}{superscript 2}) tests to determine diagnostic accuracy. Result: 304 patient records were included in the study. The fine needle aspiration cytology was determinate/diagnostic in 81.6% of cases. The study revealed the sensitivity and specificity of fine needle aspiration cytology to be 88.2% (CI 77.6-95.1%) and 94.4% (CI 90.6-97.1%), respectively. The false negative and false positive rates in this study were 2.4% and 4.4%, respectively. The positive predictive value was 80.3% (CI 68.7-89.3%), and the negative predictive value was 96.8% (CI 93.8-98.7%). The accuracy of fine needle aspiration cytology in differentiating benign from malignant thyroid lesions was 93.1%. Conclusion: FNAC demonstrated strong agreement with histopathology and remains a reliable, cost-effective first-line diagnostic tool for thyroid disease, particularly in resource-limited settings. Strengthening sample handling, ultrasound guidance, and adherence to Bethesda criteria may further improve diagnostic precision
nde558446b525: Background: Iron deficiency (ID) and iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) have global and severe health implications, and disproportionately impact women of reproductive age. Current methods of supplementing diets with iron are challenged by poor adherence and palatability, reducing effectiveness of these treatment strategies. The aim of this study is to evaluate the efficacy of a novel home beverage fortification with a mineral-enriched powder, designed to enhance bioavailability and ease of use, for the treatment of ID in women of reproductive age. Methods: This single-centre, randomised, double-blinded placebo-controlled trial will enrol 150 eligible biologically female participants with ID. Participants will be randomly assigned to the active intervention (iron/zinc-enriched powder) or control group (placebo powder) over 6 months. Primary outcomes will include change in serum ferritin (SF) concentrations and proportion of participants who remain iron deficient at 6-months. Secondary outcomes will include change in SF and haemoglobin (Hb) concentrations across timepoints, and levels of metabolites and key circulating pro-inflammatory biomarkers, changes in dietary intakes, self-reported perceptions of health, barriers to use of the powder, adherence and palatability, safety outcomes, and cost-effectiveness. Exploratory outcomes will assess the gut microbial metagenome and metabolome. Discussion: Fortification, an effective approach for the prevention of ID/IDA, has advantages over some methods of supplementation because it uses low levels of iron, minimising unpleasant side effects, does not risk toxicity, and has high acceptability and compliance rates. This mineral-enriched powder uses electrolytic iron and zinc sulphate monohydrate of a small particle size, which is less irritating to the gut, and facilitates bioavailability. Findings from the study will be shared with those affected by and involved in treating these conditions, as a novel intervention that is both effective and acceptable among women of reproductive age would help to improve treatment compliance, and ultimately, reduce ID/IDA burden. Trial registration: This trial is registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT05990166): https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05990166, August 2023.
n535d85aea36b: Background: Conventional performance metrics do not indicate whether artificial intelligence (AI)-platforms and radiologists are right or wrong on the same examinations, nor whether their non-agreement is more often beneficial or harmful. Objective: To develop, illustrate, and apply directional metrics quantifying non-agreement between radiologists and AI-platforms against a common reference standard, and to adapt a fragility-based framework for quantifying the statistical robustness of these metrics. Methods: We defined Positive Non-Agreement (PNA, AI-platform correct, radiologist incorrect), Negative Non-Agreement (NNA, radiologist correct, AI-platform incorrect), and Net Non-Agreement (NENA, their difference). Metrics were illustrated in three hypothetical scenarios of 1,000 examinations each and applied to three previously published AI-radiologist studies on pulmonary embolism and mammography. Bootstrap confidence intervals were calculated, and a reclassification fragility index (FI) quantified the minimum case reclassification needed to remove statistical support for NENA's direction. Results: In illustration, NENA was positive in two scenarios and negative in one. In the three published studies, NENA ranged from -4.18% to +10.74% and decreased consistently with increasing radiologist experience (junior residents, +6.27%; consultants, +1.45%), a gradient driven primarily by declining PNA with modest increase in NNA. The reclassification FI was defined for all three illustrative scenarios (range, 0.10%-1.70%) and for six of the seven comparisons from these studies (range, 0.34%-4.31%), but not for the weakest comparison, whose confidence interval for NENA included zero. Conclusions: PNA, NNA, and NENA provide a directional, case-level complement to conventional performance metrics for AI-radiologist non-agreement. The accompanying reclassification FI offers a statistically grounded, generalizable method for quantifying their robustness.
nb7973c94c6c3: Objectives To evaluate discrepancies between radiologists and referring physicians in the interpretation of diagnostic probabilities conveyed by common Japanese expressions used in radiology reports. Materials and Methods Fifteen expressions commonly used to convey diagnostic probabilities in radiology reports were selected by five attending radiologists. An anonymous online survey was distributed to 26 radiologists and 33 referring physicians at a single institution. Participants assigned a diagnostic probability (from 0% to 100% in 10% increments) to each expression. Differences in median probabilities between radiologists and referring physicians were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Variability in interpretation was assessed using interquartile range (IQR), with IQR [≥] 30% defined as substantial variability. Results All radiologists (26/26) and 97% of referring physicians (32/33) completed the survey. Seven of the 15 expressions showed statistically significant differences in interpretation between radiologists and referring physicians: "c/w" (80% vs. 60%; p = 0.031), the Japanese equivalents of "present" (100% vs. 100%; p = 0.024), "suspect of" (80% vs. 70%; p = 0.007), "possibly" (50% vs. 70%; p < 0.001), "unlikely" (10% vs. 10%; p = 0.022), "cannot be ruled out" (25% vs. 40%; p < 0.001), and "not inconsistent with" (80% vs. 90%; p = 0.008). Substantial variability in interpretation (IQR [≥] 30%) was observed for four expressions: "cannot be ruled out" (IQR, 10%-40%), "s/o" (IQR, 60%-90%), "c/w" (IQR, 50%-90%), and "not inconsistent with" (IQR, 70%-100%). Conclusion This study revealed that nearly half of the Japanese expressions commonly used to convey diagnostic probabilities were interpreted differently by radiologists and referring physicians. These discrepancies highlight the need for a standardized lexicon to improve clarity and consistency in radiology reporting.
n8641f445fed8: Background: Opioids remain the cornerstone of acute postoperative pain management but are associated with potentially serious adverse effects. We aimed to investigate the effect of oxycodone patient-controlled analgesia with adjunctive S-ketamine on pain after lumbar fusion surgery. Methods: In this secondary analysis, we examined oxycodone and S-ketamine exposure and PCA behaviour during the first 24 h. We assessed current pain versus subsequent PCA activity and whether the association between plasma oxycodone and adequate analgesia changed with postoperative time. Results: Plasma concentrations of administered drugs rose rapidly after PCA initiation, but variation was large. Metabolite concentrations accumulated over time. PCA attempt and delivered-dose rates decreased over postoperative time (RR 0.965 and 0.966 per hour, respectively; both P<0.001). Older age was associated with a lower delivered-dose rate (RR 0.905 per 10 years, 95% CI 0.829-0.987). Each 1-point higher current pain score was associated with more subsequent PCA attempts (RR 1.09, 95% CI 1.04-1.14) and delivered doses (RR 1.07, 95% CI 1.03-1.11). The oxycodone-analgesia association weakened over time [interaction P <0.001; odds ratios (Ors) per 10 ng/mL 1.16, 1.13, and 1.00 at 1, 4, and 24 h, respectively]. In active S-ketamine groups, including S-ketamine, norketamine, and 6-hydroxynorketamine concentrations left the pain-PCA association unchanged (RR 1.09 and 1.07) and preserved the time-dependent oxycodone association (ORs 1.30, 1.26, and 1.02). Conclusions: During PCA, drug exposure develops from patient-generated dosing histories while pain and recovery change. Current pain was associated with subsequent PCA activity, and the oxycodone-analgesia association was time-dependent.
nff336212afb6: Introduction and objectives Hydrocephalus is a common complication of aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage. This is one of several standard indications for the insertion of an external ventricular drain, but there are no standard guidelines for timing of extraventricular drain discontinuation in this population. Therefore, the study aims were to examine the 1) factors associated with extraventricular drain duration in aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage and 2) association between extraventricular drain duration and clinical and resource-based outcomes. Methods In this single centre retrospective cohort study, data for adult patients treated in the ICU between 2015-2023 with aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage and requiring an extraventricular drain were analysed. Data were extracted from both a prospective patient registry and the electronic medical record. Linear regression modelling was used to identify the factors associated with extraventricular drain duration. Measures used to examine the association between extraventricular drain duration, and the outcomes of interest included hazard ratio, relative risk, and mean differences as appropriate for a specific outcome. Results Of the participants (n=205), 68% (n = 140) were female, mean age was 60.7 (SD 13.3) years and 71% (n = 145) had a modified Fisher score of 4. Mean extraventricular drain duration was 15.3 (SD 8.6) days. The number of days mechanically ventilated and extraventricular drain challenge by clamp trial were associated with an increased duration of extraventricular drain treatment. Increased extraventricular drain duration was associated with an increased incidence of ventriculoperitoneal shunt insertion, and an increase in ICU and hospital length of stay when extraventricular drain duration exceeded 20 days. Conclusion The factors associated with an increased duration of extraventricular drain treatment were a longer duration of mechanical ventilation. The outcomes associated with an increased duration of extraventricular drain treatment were an increased incidence of ventriculoperitoneal shunt insertion, an increased incidence of ventriculitis when extraventricular drain duration exceeded 20 days, and an increase in ICU length of stay. These study findings may inform the conduct of a larger multi-centre study to examine the factors associated with duration of treatment with extraventricular drain, and outcomes associated with extraventricular drain duration.
n4413c585f97a: Objective Reducing household air pollution exposure during gestation and infancy may have longer-term benefits for child linear growth. We examined whether a liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) cookstove and fuel intervention delivered during gestation and infancy could improve height-for-age Z scores (HAZ) and reduce the risk of stunting at ages 2-5 years in India, Rwanda, and Guatemala. Materials and method The Household Air Pollution Intervention Network (HAPIN) was a randomized controlled trial that enrolled ~3200 pregnant women across Guatemala, India, Peru, and Rwanda. Women in the intervention group received an LPG cookstove and free fuel during pregnancy and until the infant reached 12 months of age. Following the HAPIN trial, we continued following children in Guatemala, India, and Rwanda (N=2169) and measured child height at ages 2, 3, 4, and 5 years (HAPIN 2.0). As prespecified in the study protocol, we used mixed-effects models, as well as linear and log-binomial regression, within the intention to treat (ITT) framework, to evaluate the interventions effect on HAZ and stunting. Subgroup analyses were performed to assess effect modification by child sex, maternal height, and intervention country. Results The intervention reduced gestational exposures to particulate matter (PM2.5: 80.7 vs 117.5 {micro}g/m3), carbon monoxide (CO: 1.3 vs 2.0 ppm), and black carbon (BC: 8.6 vs 12.1 {micro}g/m3) and infancy exposures (PM2.5: 36.9 vs 113.2 {micro}g/m3; CO: 0.60 vs 2.2 ppm). Post-trial PM2.5 exposure were similar between arms: 99.9 vs 98.7 {micro}g/m3. We found no statistically significant effect of the intervention on repeated measures of HAZ ({beta} = -0.06, 95% CI: -0.16, 0.03 p=0.204), annual HAZ, stunting, nor severe stunting at any age during the follow-up. There was no statistically significant effect modification by subgroups. Conclusion Despite substantial reductions in air pollution exposures during the trial, the LPG intervention did not improve growth or reduce stunting risk from ages 2 through 5 years in this multi-country cohort. These findings, consistent with prior results of the lack of effects on growth through 12 months, provide additional evidence that a clean cooking intervention alone may not be sufficient to address childhood stunting in low-resource settings. Future exposure-response analyses will supplement these ITT analyses.
ne9e6aefb67e3: Src family kinases (SFKs) constitute a major non-receptor tyrosine kinase class that regulate processes important for pregnancy. We profiled placental SFKs to assess cell-specific expression, tissue localization, and clinical associations in early-onset preeclampsia (PE). Placental SFK transcripts were analyzed using bulk RNA sequencing discovery (GSE203507; n=15 PE, n=15 controls) and external validation (GSE114691; n=40 PE, n=21 controls) cohorts. Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing atlases mapped cell-specific expression. Computational deconvolution and causal mediation analyses were applied to bulk datasets. Findings were cross-validated by real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR; n=9 early-onset PE, n=7 controls) and immunohistochemistry (IHC). Transcriptomic data showed that LYN was the sole SFK member consistently elevated in early-onset PE placentas across discovery (1.8-fold, FDR<0.01) and validation cohorts (2.2-fold, FDR<0.001). Elevation was verified by qPCR (p<0.0001) and remained significant after adjusting for clinical covariates. Placental LYN abundance correlated positively with maximum antepartum maternal systolic blood pressure (r=0.63, p<0.01). Single-cell transcriptome atlases demonstrated LYN enrichment in myeloid lineages, extravillous trophoblasts, and syncytiotrophoblast (SCT). Deconvolution and mediation analyses indicated that altered tissue composition and increased per-cell expression each accounted for approximately half of the PE-associated LYN increase. IHC localized Lyn protein to Hofbauer macrophages and the apical microvillar SCT membrane in PE placentas. We conclude that placental LYN expression is selectively elevated in early-onset PE and correlates with maternal blood pressure severity. Lyn localization to trophoblasts and placental immune cells suggests potential roles in mediating inflammation and hypoxia-associated signaling in PE pathogenesis.
ne05cfe2345be: Wolbachia-based interventions were less effective in achieving introgression in Rio de Janeiro than other settings. Reduced introgression occurred in locations where dengue was historically high, raising concerns of inequity. We examined factors affecting Wolbachia introgression in Rio through trajectory modeling, spatiotemporal Bayesian models, and Ae. aegypti abundance estimation. During the intervention (2017-2020), Wolbachia introgression was 26% (median; IQR,14-44%), with four distinct trajectories. Despite receiving more releases, densely populated areas with low socioeconomic status had lower introgression. In spatiotemporally explicit multivariable regressions, higher Ae. aegypti abundance, temperature, population density and lower socioeconomic status were associated with reduced introgression. Improved characterization of Ae. aegypti abundance and other structural/environmental predictors of introgression could be used to calibrate release doses to ensure equitable benefits from Wolbachia interventions.
nc44414b176fc: Background: Cross-cohort machine-learning studies of tau positivity are increasingly used to assess generalizability of Alzheimer's disease biomarker models, but apparent differences between cohorts may reflect clinical severity structure and cohort stage composition rather than genuine biological divergence. Methods: We evaluated this problem across subject-level cohorts from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS3), and the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center (NACC) using harmonized tabular predictors and a feature-block ablation framework. For ADNI and OASIS3, we performed matched-feature analyses restricted to shared harmonized variables (age, APOE e4, education, sex, the CDR(R) Dementia Staging Instrument sum-of-boxes score (CDR-SB), and the Functional Activities Questionnaire (FAQ)). Models were trained with five-fold stratified cross-validation using balanced logistic regression as the primary classifier. Random forests and extra-trees classifiers were evaluated as robustness checks and are reported in supplementary analyses. Results: In the primary matched-feature comparison, reference areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.851 for ADNI tau90, 0.860 for ADNI tau180, and 0.933 for OASIS3 tau180. Severity-only models retained 86-99% of reference performance, whereas demographic/genetic-only models retained 85-87%; bootstrap confidence intervals showed that the reference-minus-demo contrast remained positive across all primary cohorts. Before feature matching, OASIS3 showed substantially weaker demographic-only prediction (AUC approx. 0.54), attributable to missing APOE and age variables. After harmonization with a matched feature set including age, the pre-harmonization demographic gap was no longer attributable to feature availability; the residual difference was most consistent with cohort disease-stage composition asymmetry, with CDR-SB = 0 prevalence of 84.5-88.7% in OASIS3 versus 49.3-51.7% in ADNI. Conclusions: The original large ADNI-OASIS3 performance gap was largely a feature-availability artifact; after strict harmonization including age-field repair, the absolute gap narrowed and the signed ADNI-minus-OASIS3 difference reversed, with the residual difference most consistent with cohort disease-stage composition asymmetry. Clinical severity remains an important predictor across all cohorts, but the unique contributions of severity and demographic/genetic information depend strongly on stage composition. Cross-cohort biomarker modeling should account for both feature-set completeness and disease-stage composition heterogeneity, not only headline performance metrics.
n89f1d07cd824: Introduction: Neuroinflammation is a known pathophysiologic mechanism in multiple sclerosis and a proposed mechanism in fibromyalgia and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging of the translocator protein (TSPO) has been widely used to measure neuroinflammation, though second-generation ligands are highly sensitive to a single nucleotide polymorphism, rs6971, resulting in high, mixed, and low affinity binders. It is unknown whether this polymorphism is associated with neuroinflammatory disorders. Materials and Methods: Eighty-six total participant genotypes for TSPO binding affinity were identified through Sanger sequencing (30 fibromyalgia, 21 ME/CFS, 11 multiple sclerosis, and 24 healthy controls). Associations between patient group and genotype were assessed with Fishers Exact test. Associations between genotype and symptom severity from self-report questionnaires were assessed with Kruskal-Wallis tests. Results: In the present study individuals with fibromyalgia, (ME/CFS), or multiple sclerosis were more likely to have a mixed- or low-affinity genotypes compared to healthy controls. Presence of the low or mixed genotypes were also associated with greater self-reported fatigue severity and depressive symptoms. Discussion: These findings should be confirmed in larger samples but suggest functional consequences of rs6971 polymorphism that may be related to the pathophysiology of pain and fatigue illnesses.
nd2f6a0a7d16d: The World Health Organization has called for malaria vaccines with > 90% efficacy against Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) infection. The live, non-attenuated PfSPZ-CVac (chloroquine) vaccine provides the strongest protection against controlled human malaria infection (CHMI). Its 100% protective efficacy at 12 weeks against genetically distant Pf stems from a highly amplified immune stimulus. After inoculation, each invading sporozoite (SPZ) replicates up to 50,000 times within a hepatocyte. Over six days of development, these parasites express thousands of distinct proteins, presenting a vast and diverse array of antigens to the host immune system. The late liver stage parasites then rupture into the bloodstream, where they are killed by the co-administered drug, chloroquine. To engineer a Pf parasite that develops to the late liver stage like PfSPZ-CVac (chloroquine), but then arrests before transitioning to the blood stage, two genes required for transition from non-pathogenic liver to pathogenic blood stages were identified and deleted, creating late-liver stage arresting, replication-competent (LARC) PfSPZ. In a first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial, we assessed PfSPZ-LARC2 Vaccine in 75 malaria-exposed Burkinabe 1- to 48-year-olds. No vaccine-strain breakthrough blood-stage infections were detected; safety and tolerability profiles were similar in vaccinees and placebo recipients; and the highest immunogenicity was observed in the youngest recipients. Based on these findings, PfSPZ-LARC2 Vaccine has progressed to Phase 2 testing with the goal of rapidly advancing this genetically attenuated whole parasite vaccine to licensure and deployment.
n2709c681d431: High throughput sequencing necessitates robust computational tools to contextualize complex transcriptomic data. In this study, we analyzed RNA Seq data from peripheral blood of bacterial pneumonia patients and healthy controls (GEO GSE161731) to investigate systemic molecular responses to infection. Differential gene expression analysis identified significantly upregulated genes in pneumonia. We used GANGO for Gene Ontology (GO) term enrichment and BioFunctional for hierarchical exploration, providing an initial overview of affected biological processes. To deepen interpretation, we leveraged CURIE (www.curieai.tech ), an AI plat-form that cross-references GO terms with scientific literature. CURIE generates narrative explanations, link-ing molecular mechanisms, experimental evidence, and publications to each biological process, moving be-yond simple enrichment. Our combined analysis revealed a coordinated upregulation of pathways involved in DNA repair and replication, transcriptional activation, RNA processing, translation, ribosome biogenesis, mitochondrial respiration, and cofactor binding. By integrating these findings within a broad, literature-supported framework, we highlighted how multiple cellular compartments and processes collaborate to mount an effective response to infection-induced stress. This study underscores the potential of combining classical statistical enrichment with AI based interpretation for a holistic understanding of host-pathogen in-teractions at the transcriptomic level.
nc9e85b0541c6: Aims: Myocardial strain enables sensitive assessment of cardiac function, but its clinical application has largely focused on individual chambers or selected patient populations. We evaluated the feasibility and clinical relevance of fully automated multi-chamber strain assessment in consecutive patients undergoing routine transthoracic echocardiography (TTE). Methods and results: This retrospective study included 8,350 consecutive adults undergoing TTE. A hospital-wide artificial intelligence (AI)-based system automatically measured left ventricular (LV) global longitudinal strain (LVGLS), left atrial (LA) reservoir strain (LASr), and right ventricular (RV) free-wall strain (RVFWS). AI-derived LVGLS was available from at least one apical view in 97.1% of patients and from all three views in 94.8%; LASr and RVFWS were available in 94.1% and 94.5%, respectively, resulting in complete multi-chamber strain assessment in 90.3%. Strain measures showed modest correlations with conventional chamber-specific echocardiographic parameters and differential associations with clinical outcomes. Gaussian mixture modeling identified three distinct clusters characterized by preserved multi-chamber function, RV-dominant dysfunction, and pan-chamber dysfunction. Compared with the preserved cluster, pan-chamber dysfunction was associated with the highest risk of all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.44; 95% CI, 2.43-4.88; P<0.001). Prognostic associations remained evident in patients with LV ejection fraction (LVEF) [≥]50%, and cluster assignment provided incremental prognostic information beyond clinical factors, LVEF, and RV fractional area change. Conclusions: Fully automated multi-chamber strain assessment was feasible in a large consecutive TTE cohort. Integrating strain across cardiac chambers may provide complementary functional characterization and identify clinically relevant clusters with prognostic information beyond conventional assessment.
n113637ce12e2: Protein coding variants span the gamut of structural and functional effects on proteins, and they have similarly heterogeneous effects on traits. Their functional effects can be predicted and categorized, particularly using machine learning models, and integrating these predictors benefits gene discovery. However, it remains unclear how well known structural features and predicted functional scores explain the heterogeneous effects of protein coding variants on human complex traits. We introduce the Kernel Allelic Series Model (KASM), which integrates multiple functional annotations to form a kernel describing how allelic effects within a gene covary. We apply it to exome data from 26 traits and 786,871 individuals from UK Biobank and All of Us, integrating 35 annotations describing protein structure and predicting allelic effects. We estimate that rare missense heritability is at least 1.27{+/-}0.09% on average, 1.83{+/-}0.11% under our most flexible model, exceeding pLoF heritability (0.87{+/-}0.05%) and far exceeding missense burden heritability as previously estimated (0.54{+/-}0.04%). AlphaMissense is the single most enriched missense predictor, but a composite score doubles its enrichment. A series of structural features is enriched for heritability, from amino acid chemical features and structural motifs to residue contacts and protein-protein interaction interfaces. Examining pairs of variants, we find that most missense effects are modestly correlated, but an exception is when residues are close in 3D structure but distant in 1D sequence; such pairs also covary across species. Finally, we analyze individual genes and identify gene-specific enrichments, like a 95-fold enrichment among PIEZO1 hydrogen bond residues, that nominate functional hypotheses.
nb5df78faa413: Background: Placental insufficiency (PI), characterized by impaired placental function, is a leading cause of stillbirth. Although rare coding variants are known to cause a subset of stillbirths, their contribution to PI is poorly understood. Methods: We conducted a secondary analysis of stillbirth cases (N=292) of the Stillbirth Collaborative Research Network study with exome sequencing available on postmortem placental or fetal samples. PI was defined by standardized placental pathological lesions (e.g., maternal vascular malperfusion) and prespecified clinical criteria for placental dysfunction. Candidate gene-based rare-variant burden analysis was performed using the Sequence Kernel Association Test-Optimal framework, focusing on evolutionarily constrained developmental and placental-function genes. Primary analysis compared stillbirths with and without placental vascular malperfusion. Similar comparisons by clinical PI and other placental pathological lesions were conducted in secondary analysis. Results: Stillbirths with PI phenotypes demonstrated different patterns of genetic variation than stillbirths without PI. Specifically, we observed nominal differential enrichment of constrained variants in biologically prioritized placental-function genes, regulating extravillous trophoblast invasion and spiral artery remodeling (CTNND2, PHACTR1, SLIT1, VEGFA), placental angiogenesis (IGF2R, TEK), mitochondrial homeostasis (OPA1), and fetal growth (DLK1, GNAS). Secondary analyses on specific placental pathological lesions suggested recurrent enrichment of genes within similar placental developmental pathways. Conclusions: We observed nominal differential enrichment of constrained developmental and placental-function genes in stillbirths with PI compared to stillbirths without PI. The observed genetic signals across PI phenotypes suggest shared biological pathways underlie placental dysfunction. Our findings advance genotype-phenotype characterization and help prioritize candidate pathways for larger collaborative genomic and functional studies to improve stillbirth risk stratification and prevention.
n4d01109257fd: Human immune responses remain poorly characterized across Indigenous South American (ISA) populations, limiting our understanding of human immune variation. Here, we generated a single-cell transcriptional atlas of 1.4 million peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 345 individuals representing 13 South American populations, profiled at baseline and following stimulation with lipopolysaccharide, influenza A virus, or Trypanosoma cruzi. Genetic ancestry was associated with the expression of a large fraction of the transcriptome, often only after stimulation, and explained more variation than age or sex. On average, cis-eQTLs accounted for one-quarter of these ancestry-associated differences. Thousands of regulatory variants were common in ISA populations but rare or absent in European reference datasets. Integrating eQTLs with GWAS revealed stimulation-specific disease-associated regulatory variants and an enrichment of ancestry-associated expression differences among genes with colocalizing signals. Our findings highlight the importance of studying diverse populations across immune contexts to understand the genetic architecture of human immune responses.
n06cbd313ebc9: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) and early-life irregular cycles (ELIC) carry higher metabolic risks, but real-world glycemic patterns remain inadequately characterized. We analyzed 247,316 continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) days from 716 consented and enrolled participants (11/2019-08/2026) in the Apple Women's Health Study, using cluster-weighted generalized estimating equations to evaluate associations between PMOS, ELIC, and glycemic metrics. Same-day wearable-assessed physical activity, digital dietary logs, and medication health records were assessed as effect modifiers. Compared to participants without PMOS and with regular cycles, those with PMOS had higher mean glucose (6.81 mg/dL; 95% CI: -0.70, 14.72) and %observations above target range (3.77%; 95% CI: 0.04, 8.14). Estimates were smaller-in-magnitude for participants without PMOS but with ELIC, and larger for PMOS with androgen excess. Meeting activity goals, consuming protein-/fiber-rich diets, or using metformin/GLP-1 receptor agonists attenuated these associations. PMOS/ELIC were associated with unfavorable glycemic profiles, suggesting opportunities for risk identification and modification.
nb74a4dd8f54c: How inflammation is established and resolved within tissues remains a fundamental question in human biology. Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease driven by the IL-23/IL-17 pathway, with IL-17 pathway targeting biologics producing more rapid clinical improvement than IL-23 inhibitors. This difference raises the question of how IL-17 and IL-23 inhibition differentially remodel the cellular and transcriptional landscape of psoriatic skin during resolution. Here, we generated a longitudinal spatial atlas of plaque psoriasis using 2 micron high-definition spatial transcriptomics (HD-SPT), profiling 42 matched biopsies from 11 biologic treatment-naive patients before and during IL-17- or IL-23-targeted therapy. By integrating HD-SPT with a single-cell RNA-sequencing (sc-RNAseq) reference atlas, we resolved the cellular composition and spatial organization of psoriatic skin and mapped its remodeling during treatment. We identified a distinct cluster of SPRR2F+ keratinocytes (KCs) that was spatially restricted to the upper stratum granulosum at the transition to the stratum corneum and was strongly associated with inflamed psoriatic epidermis. SPRR2F+ KCs were enriched for antimicrobial and inflammatory barrier genes, including S100A8, S100A9, LCN2, IL36G, and PI3, and their abundance correlated with disease activity during treatment. In psoriasis patient-derived human epidermal KCs (P-HEK), SPRR2F knockdown attenuated inflammatory and antimicrobial transcriptional responses, supporting a functional role for SPRR2F in sustaining the inflammatory KC response in psoriasis. Longitudinal profiling further revealed distinct trajectories of tissue remodeling following IL-17 and IL-23 inhibition. Following IL-17 inhibition, SPRR2F+ KCs and their characteristic transcriptional signature resolved rapidly, whereas IL-23 inhibitors produced more gradual resolution of KC-centered transcriptional changes accompanied by broader immune and stromal remodeling. Together, these findings established the first HD-SPT atlas of a human skin disease and revealed distinct cellular and transcriptional trajectories of psoriatic skin during therapeutic resolution, identifying SPRR2F as a regulator of persistent KC inflammation.
n7c9c0b259407: Aims: To understand how users believe continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) changes their behaviour, which app features they credit, and whether endorsing more mechanisms of action (MoAs) is linked to reported diet and physical activity change. Methods: We surveyed 112 U.S. adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who had used a Dexcom or Abbott Libre CGM within 12 months. Participants rated 26 MoA statements mapped to the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behaviour (COM-B) model, identified contributing app features, and reported CGM-attributed diet and physical activity change. Logistic regression examined MoA count and COM-B domains as predictors of behaviour change. Results: Participants (mean age 54.5 years; 60.7% female) reported dietary (82.1%) and physical activity (46.4%) change and endorsed a median of 18 MoAs, most often relating to knowledge, skills and behavioural consequences. Real-time glucose and graphs were attributed to many MoAs. Each additional MoA was associated with higher odds of dietary (OR 1.27, 95% CI 1.15-1.44) and physical activity change (OR 1.27, 95% CI 1.16-1.43). Motivation made the strongest distinct contribution among COM-B domains. Conclusions: Users perceive CGM as engaging many behavioural mechanisms; endorsing more was linked to behaviour change. Motivation may be a key target for CGM-based behavioural support.
n48b041123fcf: Background: Lean Healthcare has been adopted as an approach to reducing waste, enhancing process efficiency, and optimizing clinical and administrative workflows. However, empirical evaluations aimed at establishing a causal relationship between Lean Healthcare interventions and outcomes remain limited. This evidence gap is particularly pronounced in the context of large-scale implementations in low- and middle-income countries, where more efficient allocation could yield substantial improvements in population health. Methods: We conducted an impact evaluation study employing a staggered difference-in-differences approach to estimate the effects of the Lean Healthcare in Emergency Departments (ED) initiative in the Brazilian context. The intervention was implemented between January 2017 and December 2025 across 309 hospitals. We analyzed hospital-level indicators of the number of hospitalizations and the average length of stay (in days) among patients admitted through urgent or emergency pathways. Results: Our estimates suggest that the intervention was associated with an average increase of 38.6 admissions per hospital per month (p = 0.033), corresponding to approximately a 5.9% increase relative to the monthly admission volume. We also observed a reduction of 0.184 days in the average length of stay (p = 0.058), equivalent to an approximately 3.0% decrease in hospitalization time. These effects exhibited distinct temporal dynamics: the effect on the number of hospitalizations emerged gradually and increased with the duration of the intervention, whereas the reduction in length of stay became evident earlier. Conclusion: This study provides evidence of a causal effect of Lean Healthcare implementation in emergency departments on operational performance. The simultaneous increase in admissions and reduction in length of stay suggests improved bed productivity and effective capacity without expanding physical infrastructure. These findings support the use of flow-management methodologies as an effective strategy for mitigating emergency department overcrowding while increasing service capacity.
n0adf11600c5f: Flow cytometry is central to clinical hematology, generating extensive archives comprising billions of single-cell profiles linked to expert-derived diagnostic summaries. While these records represent a largely untapped repository of collective expert knowledge, the underlying single-cell annotations required for supervised machine learning are typically not recorded in a standardized, accessible format. We present IMPGAT (implicit gating), a weakly supervised multiple-instance learning framework that reconstructs single-cell gating strategies directly from existing sample-level cell-type frequency distributions. The model utilizes an induced set attention mechanism to map single-cell marker profiles to specific cell populations, requiring neither explicit cell-level labels nor unsupervised clustering during training. We evaluate the framework on acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cohorts, totaling 711 measurements from 268 individuals and 240 million single cells. In ALL, the model's quantification of cell-type abundances shows no statistically significant difference from human inter-expert variability. In AML, the framework achieves blast quantification on par with a recently established supervised state-of-the-art model that relies on explicit single-cell annotations for training. Error analysis shows that mismatches between model predictions and expert gating primarily involve expert-labeled non-cellular events, reflecting the non-incorporation of any explicit physical prior knowledge (such as the geometric relationships traditionally used to identify doublets and debris in scatter cytograms) in model training. Conversely, model certainty correlates with phenotypic borderline cases where manual bisection is inherently difficult. Our approach enables the systematic utilization of retrospective clinical records for the development of automated, standardized gating logic and is applicable to broader high-throughput contexts, such as large-scale immune monitoring or phenotypic drug screening.
nf77a8ae4151e: Background: Privacy curtains represent a uniquely difficult infection control surface because they are frequently touched by patients, visitors, and healthcare workers, yet are difficult to disinfect using routine environmental cleaning protocols. We sought to quantify the performance of a novel automated aerosolized hydrogen peroxide system against pathogens on privacy curtains. Methods: This study was performed in an enclosed office space ({approx} 65 m^3), approximating a patient exam room. Four Bacillus atrophaeus (ATCC 9372) biological indicators (BIs) were affixed to a standard polyester privacy curtain. A single one-minute fogging phase was followed by a ten-minute contact/aeration phase (total = 11 min). Four corresponding chemical indicators measured peak airborne aerosolized hydrogen peroxide concentration, and two control BIs were placed outside of the room. Results: All four BIs demonstrated complete inactivation (no growth after seven-day incubation), representing [≥] 4-log10 spore reduction. Peak dosages reached 42 ppm nearest the aerosolized hydrogen peroxide jet outlet, with the lowest value at the near point on the back side of the curtain reaching 27 ppm (exceeding the target dosage of 25 ppm). Control exposures failed to achieve sterilization. Conclusions: A next-generation aerosolized hydrogen peroxide dry-fogging disinfection system achieved full inactivation of resistant spores on both sides of privacy curtains within a short 11-minute automated cycle.
n8d23935af521: Background: Current Lynch syndrome (LS) prediction models do not account for detailed family structure and tumour mismatch repair (MMR) status. We developed LynchRisk, a Bayesian model that estimates individualized LS probability from pedigree, cancer history and tumour MMR test results. Methods: LynchRisk combines Mendelian inheritance, age- and sex-specific cancer hazards, affected and unaffected relatives, and detailed MMR status. Parameters were derived from the literature. Results: In two simulated cases of probands with LS-associated cancers, family structure and MMR status markedly changed LS probability estimates, with implications for germline testing decisions. LynchRisk also identified situations in which a negative germline result might be considered sufficient to rule out LS or, conversely, prompt further investigations such as somatic MMR or long-read sequencing. Discussion: LynchRisk gives individualized LS probability by combining clinical, family, and tumour data at different stages of the diagnostic process. Further work will focus on recalibrating cancer hazard functions, validating model performance through simulations, and developing an R package for use by interested research groups.
n9cf3bd964f91: Objective. Temperature readings are routinely stratified by race and ethnicity, though significant group differences may reflect physiology, instrument noise, or categorization rather than biology. This study tests whether these categories partition facial infrared thermography measurements beyond individual variation and baseline device noise. Approach. A secondary analysis of thermography data (n = 951 adults) compares inner-canthus maximum (TCEmax) and full-face maximum (Tmax) temperatures across five administrative categories via one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), mixed-effects modeling, Bland-Altman analysis against oral reference, and Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis. Main results. ANOVA returns significant group differences (p < 0.001; eta-squared = 0.04 for TCEmax, 0.03 for Tmax), but the total spread (0.2 to 0.3 degrees Celsius) is comparable to device accuracy and within-subject variability. Individual variation accounts for 95% of TCEmax variance, and adding simulated Gaussian noise to participant-level temperatures (sigma = 0.10 to 0.30 degrees Celsius) preserves the complete group-mean rank order in as few as 37.5% of iterations. Significance. Testing whether a group difference survives perturbation at the scale of instrument accuracy offers a check against treating significance alone as evidence of physiology. Here, observed group differences are small relative to measurement variability, and their physiological interpretation remains uncertain, with implications for clinical tools that treat administrative categories as biologically meaningful.
n09a8be82cf8f: Background We used sequential target trial emulation (TTE) to examine associations between opioid analgesic initiation and adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes while accounting for gestational timing, time at risk, and potential confounding. Methods Using the Early Life Course platform, comprising linked population-based data for births in New South Wales, Australia (2013-2019), we emulated a new trial at each gestational week, comparing women who initiated a prescribed opioid analgesic with eligible non-initiators. Baseline covariates were balanced using inverse probability weighting. Weighted logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for neonatal outcomes, postpartum haemorrhage, and severe maternal morbidity. Pooled logistic regression estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for other maternal outcomes, combined across gestational weeks using fixed-effects meta-analysis. Sensitivity analyses assessed unmeasured confounding, exposure misclassification, and potential reverse causation. Findings Among 511,357 pregnancies, over 80% of opioid initiators received only one dispensing. Opioid initiation was not associated with increased risks of placental abruption (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.75-1.16), severe maternal morbidity (OR 1.05, 0.97-1.11), postpartum haemorrhage (OR 0.98, 0.95-1.02), low Apgar score (OR 0.99, 0.87-1.08), small for gestational age (OR 0.90, 0.85-0.95), or neonatal abstinence syndrome (OR 0.98, 0.72-1.30). Risks were elevated for PPROM (HR 1.10, 0.98-1.23), preterm birth (HR 1.26, 1.19-1.33), severe neonatal morbidity (OR 1.08, 1.02-1.17), and perinatal death (OR 1.29, 1.10-1.52). Perinatal death estimates attenuated in analyses addressing potential reverse causation. Interpretation Using a TTE approach that accounted for gestational timing and time at risk, we found no appreciable increase in most maternal or neonatal outcomes following predominantly short-term opioid initiation. Elevated risks of preterm birth, perinatal death, and third-trimester PPROM may reflect causal effects or confounding by pregnancy-related indications. Studies using time-appropriate designs and detailed information on prescribing indications and their timing are needed to clarify these associations.
nc65936921f4a: Aims Rosuvastatin is commonly co-administered with ticagrelor in patients with acute coronary syndrome. Ticagrelor inhibits breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP/ABCG2), increasing rosuvastatin exposure and potentially the risk of rhabdomyolysis. This risk may be further influenced by age and the ABCG2 c.421C>A variant. We aimed to predict optimal rosuvastatin dosing with ticagrelor in elderly patients stratified by ABCG2 genotype using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modelling Methods PBPK models for rosuvastatin and ticagrelor were developed and validated in PK-Sim using clinical data from healthy adults, elderly patients, and individuals with wild-type or homozygous ABCG2 c.421C>A genotypes. Key parameters, including BCRP catalytic activity and age-dependent declines in CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 activity, were optimized. The drug-drug interaction model incorporated competitive BCRP inhibition by ticagrelor. Rosuvastatin steady-state exposure was simulated with half or quarter standard doses during ticagrelor co-administration, and exposure matching approach was used to identify optimal dosing. Results The PBPK models demonstrated good predictive performance across populations and genotypes. In young adults with the wild-type genotype, halving the rosuvastatin dose resulted in an AUC fold change of 1.44, supporting a half-dose strategy. In young homozygous variant carriers, half-dose co-administration produced comparable exposure (AUC fold change 0.78). In elderly wild-type individuals, a four-fold dose reduction achieved comparable exposure (AUC fold change 1.06), whereas elderly variant carriers required only a half-dose reduction (1.12). Conclusions PBPK modelling supported age- and ABCG2 genotype-specific rosuvastatin dosing with ticagrelor. Elderly wild-type patients may require a further dose reduction to minimise toxicity while maintaining therapeutic exposure.
n22583a72df07: Background: The first thousand days are a sensitive window for child health and social health inequalities. When routine care falls short, parents of young children turn to online sources and, recently, to generative artificial intelligence (AI). Evidence on their concerns, child-health literacy, and AI use is scarce. Objective: To describe health informational needs and concerns, child-health literacy, and use of AI for child-health questions, including differences by parental role and parity, among parents of young children. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, two anonymous self-administered online questionnaires were disseminated through a digital health application between May 12 and June 11, 2026, to French-speaking parents of at least one child aged 0 to 47 months in France. Questionnaire 1 covered unmet information needs, concerns across 16 topics, perceived intra-couple concordance, and confidence in routine care. Questionnaire 2 covered a four-item child-health literacy quiz and AI use (frequency, topics, 12-month trend, barriers, trust conditions, perceived effect on consultations, and disclosure). Results: In total, 12,634 parents responded (Questionnaire 1, n=5,410; Questionnaire 2, n=7,224), mostly mothers (94.6% and 92.9%). Most (61.8%) had searched for information without finding a clear, reliable answer, selecting a median of 4 (Interquartile range [IQR] 3-7) over 16 topics. Leading concerns were sleep (51.3%), nutrition (48.1%), and education (i.e., upbringing and behavior) (47.8%). Mothers were nearly twice as likely as fathers to select accident prevention (26.5% vs 16.3%) and parental mental health (38.7% vs 28.6%); first-time parents selected most topics more often than experienced parents, most markedly dental hygiene (43.8% vs 27.6%). The median child-health literacy score was 3 (IQR 3-4) on a 0-to-4 quiz, with 19.9% of parents scoring 2 or below; tooth-brushing age was the weakest item (68.4% correct). Mothers outscored fathers on every item. More than half of parents (54.2%) had used AI for a child-health question, 11.2% weekly; among those reporting a trend, 68.3% had increased AI use for child-health questions over the year and 6.2% decreased it. The main barriers to AI use were a preference for professionals (55.9%) and reliability concerns (48.7%); trust depended most on medical oversight of the tool (76.6%). AI use appeared additive, with 66.8% reporting no change in healthcare visit frequency. One third (35.5%) had told an AI something shared with neither a professional nor their network, rising to 64.1% among regular users. Conclusions: Parental informational needs were widespread and frequently unmet. AI has become a common and fast-rising source for child-health questions, at times a confidential one, used alongside rather than instead of professionals. Child-health literacy was generally high but uneven, with oral health the clearest gap. Strengths include the sample size and early-generative-AI timing; limitations include the cross-sectional design, self-report, digital-recruitment selection bias, and the small proportion of fathers.
n092455b90abe: Multi-token prediction (MTP) can accelerate language-model decoding by drafting several tokens and verifying them in a single target-model pass. However, the best speculation horizon changes with context: longer drafts offer greater amortization when reliable, but can waste compute on suffixes discarded after a rejection. Unlike autoregressive drafting, where a stopping rule can decide token by token, MTP must fix the horizon before drafting, as all heads fire in the same forward pass. We therefore formulate horizon selection as an online control problem, using verification feedback to learn how far the draft can be trusted in each context, and introduce Adaptive Multi-Token Prediction (AMTP): a lightweight controller that requires no retraining and leaves the exact verifier unchanged. To guide horizon selection, we characterize the expected number of tokens committed at each horizon via acceptance survival, the probability that a draft prefix is fully accepted. Before each round, AMTP predicts how far the draft is likely to survive and picks the horizon with the highest expected tokens per second, learning freely from every verification pass. Theoretically, we show that any online learner's prediction error translates into throughput regret against the best horizon for each context, and in turn into a bound on wall-clock completion time. With online gradient descent, this regret is sublinear. Across five draft-target pairings built on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with Medusa heads, Meta's MTP models, and Qwen3-4B-Inst-2507-MTP, evaluated on AIME 2025 and GSM8K, AMTP decodes up to 4.1x faster than standard decoding and matches or outperforms the fixed window in 8 of 10 settings, with throughput gains of up to 10%.
na5aeaeece5cf: Visual anomaly detection aims to detect abnormal objects, while anomaly samples are often scarce during model training. Assembling multiple pretrained detectors can help by leveraging their transferable image scores and anomaly maps. However, most existing ensemble methods apply fixed fusion rules over saved predictions which struggle when pretrained detectors clearly disagree due to different training objectives, priors, and visual representations. To this end, we design AnomalyAgent, a post-training fusion framework for accurate visual anomaly detection. AnomalyAgent aligns heterogeneous scores and maps, summarizes score- and region-level disagreement, and treats fusion as a finite action-selection problem. It implements two types of actions: 1) score actions that determine how to fuse image-level detector confidence via consensus, robust aggregation, detector weighting, or score-map consistency; 2) map actions that fuse dense anomaly responses via consensus, detector weighting, geometric aggregation, or disagreement correction. A constrained vision-language model (VLM) is introduced to inspect high-conflict samples and select valid score action and map action to produce the final prediction. We evaluate AnomalyAgent on MVTec AD and VisA as primary benchmarks, together with seven additional public anomaly benchmarks and Real-IAD for large-scale score-level evaluation. Across these benchmarks, AnomalyAgent consistently improves over equal-weight fusion and achieves the best mean image AUROC and pixel AP among the compared fusion methods on MVTec AD and VisA, while demonstrating robust transfer across additional anomaly domains.
nad43189908de: The static relative permittivity is an important property in thermodynamic modeling, electrochemistry, and solvent design, but predicting it directly from molecular structure remains challenging because both electronic polarization and molecular dipole orientation contribute to the measured response. Here, we introduce CRAFT-ε (Conformer-Resolved Atom- and Fragment-based Theory for ε), a conformer-resolved molecular descriptor model for predicting the static relative permittivity of neutral pure liquids. Conformer free energies, molecular dipoles, and atom-resolved polarizabilities are obtained from a GFN2-xTB/ALPB 10 workflow. The molecular dipole is decomposed into chemically defined polar-fragment vectors, allowing fitted corrections to retain both the magnitude and relative orientation of local dipolar contributions. Electronic and orientational polarization are combined with a group-contribution molar volume in the Onsager-Kirkwood-Fröhlich relation. A staged parameterization with 41 parameters is applied to nonpolar, polar, and hydrogen-bonding compounds. For 1393 liquids with permittivities between 1.5 and 183, CRAFT-ε reaches a five-fold cross-validated average absolute deviation of 2.40 ({R^2} = 0.93). Conformational averaging 15 is essential for liquids with several polar groups. Compared with an established fragment-based model with 139 parameters, it reaches a similar cross-validated RMSE (3.65 versus 3.41) with about a quarter of the parameters and applies to every liquid of the dataset. The resulting framework provides a computationally inexpensive route from molecular structure to liquid dielectric response and forms a basis for later application to solvent mixtures and electrolyte systems.
neebfac4a1459: Weakly hydrated anions tend to partition to macromolecular surfaces, leading to salting-in at low salt concentrations. Recent studies have linked this partitioning to disruption of the interfacial water network. Here, we investigate the role of interfacial-water-network disruption as an indirect driving force for the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions and its interplay with direct solute-anion and anion-cation interactions using computer simulations. We study the adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ and I$^{-}$ ions on a model extended solute that interacts with water and ions only via van der Waals interactions. To probe the indirect contribution, we increase the effective solute size while simultaneously decreasing the attractive solute-water and solute-ion interactions, resulting in progressively greater disorder in the interfacial water network in pure aqueous solutions. Our results show that iodide adsorption increases despite weaker direct solute-iodide interactions and correlates with greater disruption of the interfacial water network, although iodide remains depleted overall. In contrast, preferential adsorption of SCN$^{-}$ decreases, but the rate of decrease becomes smaller at higher levels of interfacial-water-network disorder. This suggests that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption partly compensates for the decrease in SCN$^{-}$ adsorption caused by weaker direct solute-SCN$^{-}$ interactions. Our results highlight that the indirect contribution associated with interfacial-water-network disruption promotes the adsorption of weakly hydrated anions on macromolecular surfaces, while the extent of adsorption also depends on direct solute-ion interactions and anion-cation pairing. This interplay may be particularly important in mixed-salt solutions, where the presence of strongly hydrated anions can also disrupt the interfacial water network.
n9cc651d17707: Lateral fluorination has emerged as a powerful design variable in the design of polar liquid crystals, but its interplay with terminal-group identity remains poorly understood. Here we report a 40-member matrix of biphenyl-ester-phenyl mesogens that independently varies lateral core fluorination and terminal-group identity. Increasing lateral fluorination generally suppresses apolar mesophases and clearing points, however this same change can enable polar nematic phase behaviour in conjunction with suitable terminal units. Graph Fourier analysis of conformer averaged atomic charges shows polar materials occupy a high-frequency region of charge-spectral space, consistent with a bond-scale electrostatic motif. Different terminal units can bias this towards higher or lower frequencies, and in doing so can enable polar order to emerge.
n75324d8be99b: Real-time hybrid-functional calculations require repeated reconstruction of nonlocal exchange, whose cost grows rapidly with Brillouin-zone sampling. We develop two methods to improve the efficiency of time evolution and spatial processing. The first learns the time evolution of adaptively compressed exchange (ACE) factors and predicts their updates, reducing the frequency of explicit reconstruction. The second uses crystal symmetry to reuse exchange fast Fourier transforms (FFTs) among equivalent real-space points. This symmetry-based FFT reuse (SBFR) reduces the number of FFTs while retaining the full $\bm k$-point sum. The methods can be used with a variety of hybrid functionals, and we use HSE06 in this work. Relative to an ACE reference using full-row mesh FFTs, learned prediction provides more than fivefold acceleration, SBFR more than fourteenfold, and their combination more than sixty-threefold. The combined method shows efficient parallel scaling. After learning, propagation takes less than 0.5 s per step. The reduced computational cost allows us to study nonlinear and nonequilibrium electron dynamics with hybrid functionals and to examine the role of excitonic effects in semiconductors and insulators.
n97219530d00f: Electrons in graphene move like massless relativistic particles, making them exceptionally mobile but difficult to trap because Klein tunnelling permits unimpeded passage through electrostatic barriers. This challenge extends to atomic collapse and hadron confinement. Twisted trilayers form Bernal and rhombohedral domains joined by smooth boundaries, bringing their carriers into contact. Here we show that a new mechanism, distinct from established approaches, confines massless fermions in equilateral triangular Bernal domains without mass barriers, bulk gaps or physical edges. Simulations and analytical modeling reveal that massless carriers have no adiabatic continuation into rhombohedral domains, while escape through nonadiabatic coupling to massive carriers is exponentially suppressed by smooth stacking variation. Perfect reflection in the adiabatic limit turns Bernal domains into quantum cavities in a gapless, edgeless metal. Striking density-of-states oscillations encode Eisenstein-integer arithmetic, linking energies and degeneracies to norms and prime factorizations. These findings bring relativistic confinement and number theory into experimentally accessible electronic spectra.
nc0f96031da6e: Distinguishing atomic species is an ongoing challenge in the field of scanning probe microscopy. Typically, atomic force microscopy makes use of electrostatic interactions to perform atomic identification. Here we perform lateral force microscopy (LFM) measurements with a CO terminated tip of a partially oxidized Cu(110) surface and show clear differences between the metal and oxygen sites over a large z-range. This allows for atomic identification on a typical metal oxide. Density functional theory based calculations show that the tip-sample interaction is dominated by short-ranged orbital interactions and that the electrostatic contribution is negligible. At small tip-sample distances, LFM can probe the Prandtl-Tomlinson stick-slip mechanism on the single-atom scale. It is visible as a striking asymmetry in the forward and backward scan directions, experimentally revealing this fundamental model for nanotribology on the single-atom scale.
n617fdf4748d9: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. Our results provide a general strategy for exploring and manipulating topological optical states.
n694a15db0723: Understanding the three-dimensional (3D) quantum Hall effect, characterized by a Chern vector rather than a single Chern number, has been a central pursuit in topological physics. While quantized Hall transport is established for the special case with one nonzero Chern component, recent realizations of more general Chern-vector states raise a fundamental question: how does such topology protect quantized transport? Here, we predict a distinct 3D quantized Hall effect protected by $\mathbf{C}=(0,m,n)$. For samples with dimensions $L_y$ and $L_z$, global topology enforces collective quantization of $mL_y+nL_z$, despite the fragility of individual edge modes to disorder. This reveals a novel transport regime in which robust quantization emerges as a holistic property of a unified chiral network,rather than of its constituent modes. Crucially, this collective response manifests as a quantized Hall conductance $G_{xy}=\pm(mL_y+nL_z)e^2/h$, with a distinctive dependence on both Chern-vector components and sample dimensions. We propose candidate materials to facilitate experimental observation.
n9c785242bcbe: The magnetic ground states of rare-earth frustrated magnets can be governed by competing energy scales arising from crystal-field anisotropy, exchange interactions, and long-range dipolar interactions. Here we investigate this interplay in the triangular-lattice antiferromagnet NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$ by combining magnetization, specific heat, and neutron scattering measurements. Neutron powder diffraction resolves rotations of the ErO$_6$ octahedra and supports the lower-symmetry $R\bar{3}$ structure over the previously proposed $R\bar{3}m$ model. Magnetization measurements and inelastic neutron scattering establish an effective spin-1/2 description of its low-temperature magnetism with pronounced easy-axis anisotropy, arising from a well-isolated Kramers ground-state doublet separated from the first excited crystal-electric-field level by approximately 4 meV. Below $T_{\rm N}=0.1$ K, single-crystal neutron diffraction reveals A-type antiferromagnetic order with the ordered moment predominantly oriented within the $ab$ plane, despite the pronounced paramagnetic easy-axis anisotropy. The estimated dipolar interaction scale is comparable to $T_{\rm N}$, and classical dipolar-energy calculations for the observed stacking pattern favor an in-plane moment orientation. These results reveal contrasting crystal-field and dipolar anisotropies in determining the magnetic ground state of NaBaEr(BO$_3$)$_2$.
na77f52ac0863: Three-dimensional time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (3D ToF-SIMS) builds chemical volumes by stacking images acquired between sputter cycles. Standard reconstruction assumes a flat starting surface and a single sputter rate, so samples with topography, or with layers that sputter at different rates, yield distorted interface positions and depth scales. This article is a practical guide to correcting these artifacts. We group the available corrections by the information they need: the SIMS data alone, atomic force microscopy (AFM) topography before and after the profile, or AFM topography also at intermediate stages. All three are applied to a model Pt/TaOx/Ta/Pt/Ti crossbar memristor device measured with in situ SIMS/AFM at ten stages, together with the data preparation they share. Each correction method is evaluated using the known device geometry and the measured surface evolution. The data-only correction requires no additional instrumentation and restores relative topography, but its depth scale depends on nominal layer thicknesses and remains unconstrained below the last calibrated interface. AFM before and after the profile fixes the start and end surfaces but assumes uniform sputtering in between, which fails next to the device, where the surroundings change material during the profile. Multi-stage AFM correction follows these changes and reproduces the structure of the device, at the cost of instrument time and repeated imaging of a partially sputtered surface. A decision flowchart and a checklist help readers choose, validate and report a correction.
nac1c4183fc91: $\mathrm{NiPS_3}$ has attracted considerable attention, yet the origin of its intriguing magnetic behaviors remains elusive due to limited insight into its low-energy anisotropy. Here, high-field torque magnetometry measurements are performed, revealing a previously unrecognized anisotropic spin response that reflects interaction terms beyond the standard XY or XXZ models. In combination with relativistic density functional theory calculations and magnetic force response theory, an effective low-energy spin Hamiltonian is constructed, elucidating not only the observed anomalous magnetic behavior but also other recent experiments. Remarkably, the magnetic dipole interaction and the associated spin-flop transition play a crucial role in driving the deviation from two-dimensional spin alignment, providing direct insight into the underlying anisotropic energy hierarchy. The generalized Hamiltonian can serve as the important fundamental ground for future study, and our approach adopted here will hopefully be relevant to many other related material systems.
n2b3ea51dfbc7: Deep generative modeling has achieved remarkable progress in crystal generation. Given the rich symmetries inherent in crystalline structures, recent work has sought to explicitly incorporate space-group symmetry into generative models, enabling more effective exploration of novel symmetry templates. Yet introducing symmetry templates increases the combinatorial complexity of stoichiometric relationships between atomic species and crystallographic sites, while creating a fundamental tension between flexible exploration of discrete crystallographic templates and faithful realization of these templates as continuous three-dimensional structures. To address these challenges, we propose CrystalAR, a unified autoregressive framework that models Wyckoff symmetry templates and complete crystal structures within a single generative sequence. Specifically, CrystalAR reformulates continuous coordinate generation as a symmetry-conditioned hierarchy of discrete spatial localization decisions, autoregressively refining the positions of all symmetry-inequivalent sites across resolution levels while jointly modeling their spatial configuration within each level. This discrete hierarchical formulation further enables constraint-aware search over both crystallographic templates and geometric realizations. As a result, CrystalAR retains strong symmetry-template generation capability while achieving competitive de novo generation performance and template-free crystal structure prediction (CSP) accuracy. These results suggest that symmetry-template generation can be retained alongside broadly competitive de novo generation performance and competitive CSP without reliance on symmetry templates retrieved from prior data, providing a promising alternative paradigm for symmetry-preserving crystal generation.
n5d66862ecd57: Operando and in-situ experiments extend powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) to materials that evolve during experiments, producing series of hundreds or thousands of patterns. Such series are commonly refined one pattern at a time, so weak signals give noisy structural trajectories. Parametric refinement instead fits a shared model to all patterns, but with most existing programs, changing the model or fitting it efficiently remains challenging. Here, we introduce diffPXRD, a differentiable PXRD engine in PyTorch. diffPXRD calculates derivatives by automatic differentiation, so a shared model can be changed without new derivative code. Batched fitting is also more than seven times faster than serial fitting. In an operando cathode series, a shared lattice model can reduce lattice-parameter variability by 68.4% when 10% of the photon counts are retained. We also show shared models can describe the precipitation and dissolution of Li2S and reconstruct collective atomic displacements in Ca3Ti2O7.
